Almost every business that sells to customers in India already uses WhatsApp. The question is not whether to use it, but which version. Meta offers two quite different products for businesses: the free WhatsApp Business app and the WhatsApp Business Platform, usually called the WhatsApp Business API. This guide explains the difference in plain terms and helps you decide when it is time to move.

The WhatsApp Business app

The WhatsApp Business app is a free app you install on a phone. It adds business features to normal WhatsApp:

  • A business profile with address, hours and website
  • Quick replies, a greeting message and an away message
  • Labels to organise chats
  • A simple product catalogue

It works well for a single owner or a very small team. The limits appear as you grow: the number lives on one phone (plus a small number of linked devices), there is no real automation beyond simple greetings, and it does not connect to other business software in a meaningful way. When that phone is busy, lost or with someone on leave, the business stops answering.

The WhatsApp Business API (WhatsApp Business Platform)

The API is not an app you download. It is a service from Meta that business software connects to. Your team then uses WhatsApp through that software, for example a CRM, instead of through a phone.

This changes what is possible:

  • Whole-team access. Many staff can work on the same business number at the same time, each from their own login.
  • Automation and chatbots. New messages can be answered instantly with buttons, menus and AI-assisted replies.
  • Scheduled follow-ups and reminders. Messages can be sent automatically at the right time, using message templates approved by Meta.
  • Integration. Chats, leads, payments and customer records live together in your CRM.
  • Click-to-WhatsApp ads. Leads from WhatsApp ads arrive directly in the system and can be assigned to staff automatically.
  • Voice. Voice messages and WhatsApp voice calls can be handled inside connected software, so calls are part of the customer history.

A few things to know about the API

Templates and the 24-hour window

When a customer messages you, you can reply freely for a limited time. To start a conversation yourself, for example a follow-up or a reminder, you send a message template that Meta has approved in advance. Good CRM software manages these templates for you.

Pricing

Meta charges for certain business-initiated messages, and the rates depend on the message category and the customer's country. Meta updates its pricing from time to time, so check the current rates on Meta's official pages when you plan your budget.

Business verification

To use the API at scale, your business is normally verified in Meta Business Manager. This is a one-time process that confirms your company details.

When should you move to the API?

Consider moving when one or more of these is true:

  • More than one or two people need to answer customers on WhatsApp.
  • You run Click-to-WhatsApp or lead ads and leads are being missed or answered late.
  • Your team spends hours each day on follow-ups and reminders.
  • You want every chat, call and payment connected to a customer record.

Frequently asked questions

Is the WhatsApp Business API free?

No. Meta charges for some message types, mainly messages that the business starts, and you also need software such as a CRM to use the API. Check Meta's official pricing for current rates.

Can many staff use one WhatsApp number with the API?

Yes. With the API, many staff can work on the same business number at the same time through connected software, each with their own login.

Can I make WhatsApp voice calls through the API?

Yes, connected business software can handle WhatsApp voice calls and voice messages, so calls are recorded as part of the customer's history.

Do I need a verified business to use the API?

Meta normally asks businesses to complete business verification in Meta Business Manager to use the WhatsApp Business Platform at scale.
